note: Every top-level integer constant in every backend gate script, with the direction it may move. check:baseline-integrity fails on an unregistered constant (which is what a rename looks like), a stale registration (the other half of a rename), and any move in the unsafe direction. ratchet = may only decrease. floor = may only increase; lowering a floor is how a gate goes blind while printing OK. pinned = may not change without re-registering, used where the safe direction is genuinely not obvious.

MAX_HOPS.reason: New constant, not a rename — registered 2026-09-04 when this gate's reach went from 2 of 336 paginated GETs to the whole corpus. It caps how many times the payload classifier will follow a return expression through a callback wrapper (runInTenantTransaction, cachedVersioned, withTenant and friends) before giving up and reporting `unresolved`. A ratchet because RAISING it is the dangerous direction: a deeper walk resolves more handlers and so makes the gate look better without any code improving, and an unbounded walk would recurse on a cyclic re-export. RESPONSE_SCHEMA_UNCOVERED_CEILING.owner: every module lane that owns a controller; coordinated by the API contract owner (ticket 04)
RESPONSE_SCHEMA_UNCOVERED_CEILING.reason: Operations declaring NO response body schema. Registered 2026-09-03 by v2 ticket 30 at the TRUE measured figure, 3,617 of 3,642 uncovered (25 covered, 0.69%). The gate previously required 100% and reported 3642/3642 (100%) -- because its predicate accepted a bare 2xx response KEY, which NestJS auto-generates with no content for every handler, so the condition was true for every operation the moment the document was generated. Actual coverage of the property it claimed was 1 in 3,642 (0.027%). This is NOT a baseline raised to turn a regression green: it is the first honest measurement of a number that was never measured, and the 100%% requirement was NOT restored only because demanding it would red the pipeline on ~3,617 handlers across every module lane. Lower it as coverage lands; raising it retires the rule by arithmetic. LOWERED 3617 -> 3613 on 2026-09-04 by v2 ticket 04: the ratchet had been BREACHED at 3,621 because six newly added operations carried no response schema, and it was not raised to absorb them -- ten handlers were given a real @ResponseSchema(...) instead (POST/PUT /calendar/events, PATCH/DELETE /calendar/events/{eventId}/occurrences/{occurrenceStart}, and all six /platform/operator-access operations), each compared against the real handler return by ResponseContractInterceptor under NODE_ENV=test. 3,613 was MEASURED by rebuilding the document in memory from the working tree via generateOpenApiJson() and running this gate's own predicate over it (3,651 operations, 38 covered). It is provisional in one respect and the next reader must know it: the COMMITTED openapi.json still predates both those schemas and three routes other lanes added, so it measures 3,621 and this gate stays RED until the single end-of-wave regenerate -- at which point the figure must be RE-MEASURED and lowered again if it lands below 3,613, never raised if it lands above. CLOSED 2026-09-07: LOWERED 3611 -> 0. Every one of the 3,666 operations now declares a response body schema, measured by regenerating openapi.json from the working tree and running this gate over it. Two mechanisms were added to make the count honest rather than merely large: @NoContentResponse() stamps a 204 as deliberate and fails CLOSED (a handler that claims no content while carrying a @ResponseSchema, or without @HttpCode(204), ends up with NO contract rather than a false one), and isVacuousSchema() rejects a root that says nothing -- {}, a bare {type:"object"}, an open additionalProperties record, an array of those, or an allOf/anyOf/oneOf whose every member is vacuous -- so a handler cannot be counted as covered by declaring z.record(z.string(), z.unknown()). Three schemas that had been parked as loose records were written out against their real handler returns in the same change (CRM import preview, leads import batch, org-hierarchy tree). The ceiling is now a hard 100% requirement: any new handler without a response contract reds this gate.

CONDITIONAL_BASELINE.reason: Runtime-selected describes. LOWERED 29 -> 20 on 2026-09-07, and the count itself went 76 -> 20, because the class was RETIRED rather than repriced. The 56 *.db.spec.ts files each opened with `const describeDb = ENABLED && DB_URL ? describe : describe.skip`; that ternary existed only because the default jest run walked those files on machines with no database. They are now selected by suite instead, exactly as *.e2e-spec.ts already was — jest-db.json selects the 56, `pnpm test:db-specs` runs them, and the default jest config ignores \.db\.spec\.ts$ — so the gate became redundant and was deleted. Each spec now THROWS naming the variable it needs when its database is absent, so a missing prerequisite is a red suite and can no longer skip. 19 of the 56 also carried a hermetic half that ran in the default suite; that half was split into a sibling *.spec.ts rather than allowed to fall out of the run silently (16 files, 71 tests, all passing with no database, counted before and after). The 20 survivors are genuinely infrastructure-gated: 9 *.eval.spec.ts needing an AI provider key, 6 src/degradation/** needing a real S3/Ably/read-replica, and the seeded-E2E and perf specs that need specific tenant fixtures to mean anything. This also dissolves the recorded tension with PRD-C018: a new *.db.spec.ts now joins jest-db.json and adds nothing to this class. A ratchet is lowered to the measured value, never raised to fit one.

Reconciled 2026-09-07 after re-proving the mechanism: one planted `as number` moved the total 407 -> 408 and removing it returned it to 407, so the counter counts and the tree is genuinely at 407, down from the four figures the 1000 was set against. Lowered 400 -> 380 on 2026-09-08 for the same reason and to the same standard, measured 407 -> 394. The drop is a GAIN banked, not a regression: the N+1 batching pass rewrote four files and the casts went with the code that needed them - /leads/lead-triggers.ts 9 -> 2, where the round-robin read-modify-write became a single upsert and the per-rule assignment loop became a decided AssignmentPlan; /cron/cron-billing.service.ts 2 -> 0 and /hr/directory/employee-bulk-onboarding.service.ts 1 -> 0, whose per-row loops became preloaded maps plus one batched write; and /cron/cron-projects.service.ts 3 -> 0, where three non-null `!` were replaced by a real `template is RunnableTemplate` type predicate rather than moved. Verified against current source at AST level before the ledger was touched, and the assertions did not relocate: all six new bulk-onboarding/ helper files hold zero, and the gate reported zero grown and zero added files across the whole 4,080-file corpus. Bite proof re-run before this move, not inherited: one planted `BATCH_SIZE as number` in cron-projects.service.ts took the total 394 -> 395, `as X` 273 -> 274 and the file count 221 -> 222 and flipped that file's ledger verdict from "no plain assertion left" to "tree 1"; removing it returned all four.

MAX_SUPPRESSED_UNBOUNDED.reason: Unbounded reads hidden behind a FALSE-POSITIVE verdict, counted as instances. A verdict is keyed per FILE and carries one sentence, so a read added to an already-blessed file inherits a justification never written about it - /clients/clients.service.ts' unbounded CSV export of every client in the org sat under 'client reads bounded by clientId+orgId (single-record lookups)' and no other check in the gate moved. Measured at 651 with no headroom; banked 651 -> 646 on 2026-09-06 after the gate reported the improvement. RAISED 646 -> 650 on 2026-09-08, the first upward move; every previous one was downward. The N+1 pass replaced per-row loops with batched statements, so round trips fell by orders of magnitude while the count of statements without a literal .limit() rose by four - one batched read replaces N reads that each carried .limit(1). The newly hidden reads, named as this reason requires: (1,2) /cron/cron-billing.service.ts - the trial_ends_at window read and the dunning milestone read, which replaced three windowed SELECTs per org and up to 3R milestone INSERTs; (3,4) /invoices/invoices-lifecycle.service.ts - loadFallbackRecipients, one ranked row_number() read capped at 5 recipients per org, which replaced one interleaved SELECT per overdue invoice; (5,6) @common/hr/sync-canonical-reporting-line.ts - the employments join at :32 and the open-lines read at :185 in syncCanonicalReportingLines, where a limit was REFUSED rather than forgotten: the only candidate bound is the id-set length, and if one person held two primary employments it would silently drop a different user's row and corrupt effective-dated reporting history, which the per-user .limit(1) it replaced could never do; (7) /gdpr/gdpr-sync-export-fetchers.ts - the ranked .as() subquery, which is a definition rather than an executed statement, and whose outer read carries an exact persons x (cap+1) limit. Offset by three reads the same pass removed: /cron/cron-notifications.service.ts (fan-out moved into the database), /kb/wiki/kb-page-duplicate.service.ts (the unscoped root re-read is gone) and /leads/lead-triggers.ts (the round-robin read-modify-write became one upsert). Net +4. Four further reads were BOUNDED in code in the same pass rather than suppressed, so they are absent from this number: both /ai/core/services/crm-tasks.service.ts reads now limit to their id-set length, the gdpr outer read to persons x (cap+1), and /cron/cron-projects.service.ts' status read uses DISTINCT ON (project_id) with a limit of the project count. Lower this the moment any of the seven above is bounded. Lowered 650 -> 649 on 2026-09-08: the dunning milestone read moved into /cron/cron-billing-dunning.ts when cron-billing.service.ts was split, and was BOUNDED rather than re-suppressed. It had read every dunning attempt ever recorded for the batch subscriptions while planAttempts only ever consults an entry current pastDueAt, so its row count grew with account age rather than with the batch; narrowing it to the periods actually in play caps it at one row per (entry, milestone) and the limit now states that. Six newly hidden reads remain.
